reviewed_by: Claude review of companion stream and fork edge cases
reason: Two api.py routes mishandled predictable failures. companion_stream called browser_companion.session(session_id) inside a try whose except tuple did not include NotFoundError, so a stale tab opening the stream for a removed companion session raised out of the handler before accept: an ASGI denial instead of the 4404 close every other websocket route sends for a missing record. fork_chat_session created the vendor HarnessSession branch (status starting) before ChatService.fork_session validated the request, so a fork rejected for an active turn or a boundary from another conversation answered 409 and left one orphaned HarnessSession per attempt. The stream now closes 4404 for a missing session, and a failed conversation fork deletes the vendor branch it created before re-raising. test_api gains the 4404 case (a WebSocketDenialResponse on main); test_chat_api gains a harness fork with a foreign boundary asserting 409 and exactly the original vendor session left (two on main). Both files' existing cases cover the neighbouring websocket auth, run-event and chat session routes.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (matched through api.py) is the real-Core journey suite and does not open a stream for a removed companion session or fork a harness conversation with a foreign boundary; the Python tests drive both routes through TestClient. No full suites.
